items.prompt: Black to move. White's king is safe on g1 and no attack on it is possible yet. Find a move that develops a piece or hits the centre and keeps the position level.

claims.statement: Ng4, Nxd4, Bd7, Re8 and d5 are each within 45 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16).
White's king is on the kingside.

hints: White's king sits on g1 behind unmoved pawns. What does that say about speed?
Several developing or central moves are equally good; the knight on d4 and the centre offer targets.
Ng4, Nxd4, Bd7, Re8 or d5.
items.explain: Ng4, Nxd4, Bd7, Re8 and d5 each score within 45 centipawns of the engine's best move at depth 16, so Black has no need to rush an attack while White's king stays at home.

items.prompt: White to move after ...Bg4 (White's queen is on d1, the knight on b3). Does capturing on g4 win a piece (net, with best play)?

claims.statement: Bxg4 is the engine's top move (depth 16).
The engine (depth 16) rates the position at least three pawns better for White.
The white queen is on d1.

hints: After Bxg4 Nxg4, who attacks the knight on g4?
Look at the diagonal from d1 to g4: is anything in the way?
The queen takes the knight on g4 and nothing recaptures.
items.explain: After Bxg4 the only recapture is the knight, and the queen on d1 takes it for free: White gains a piece.

items.prompt: White to move after ...Bg4 (the queen has been moved to d2; everything else as before). Does capturing on g4 win a piece (net, with best play)?

claims.statement: Bxg4 wins at most one pawn here along the engine's line (depth 16): it does not win a piece.
The white queen is on d2.

hints: Compare with the previous position. What moved?
From d2 the queen no longer looks along the diagonal to g4.
After Bxg4 Nxg4 nothing attacks the knight.
items.explain: With the queen on d2 nothing attacks a knight that recaptures on g4, so Bxg4 Nxg4 is an even bishop trade, not a won piece (and the knight then attacks the bishop on e3). White's best here is still f3, about 60 centipawns at depth 16 [V]. The square of the queen decides.

items.prompt: White to move after ...Bg4. This time Black's a-pawn stands on a6 and White's queen is on d1. Does capturing on g4 win a piece (net, with best play)?

claims.statement: Bxg4 wins at least a piece along the engine's line (depth 16).
Black's pawn is on a6 and the white queen on d1.

hints: Which pieces take part in the capture on g4?
Is the a-pawn on any of the lines from d1 to g4?
Which pieces take part in the capture on g4?
items.explain: The a-pawn takes no part: after Bxg4 Nxg4 the queen on d1 still takes the knight, so White gains a piece.

The white bishop stands on e3.

All three White pieces are on their Yugoslav squares, so the answer is yes.
items.explain: The pawn is on f3, the bishop on e3 and the queen on d2, with Black's bishop on g7: the Yugoslav setup, reached here by 6.f3 first. Move order can differ; the position is what counts.

items.prompt: Is this the Yugoslav Attack setup (pawn on f3, bishop on e3, queen on d2, Black's bishop on g7)?

claims.statement: The f3 square is empty: White's f-pawn is still on f2.
A white pawn stands on f2.
White's bishop stands on e2.

Check the f-file pawn and the bishop on e2.

items.explain: The pawn is still on f2. Bishop and queen stand on their Yugoslav squares, so White can play f3 next and reach the Yugoslav setup by transposition (the engine rates f3 as the top move here [V]); as it stands the setup is not complete, and White's king has not yet chosen a side.

Nxe4 is at least 250 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: The pawn on e4 is attacked once and guarded once.

Develop with Bg7 or Bd7.
items.explain: Bg7 and Bd7 are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move at depth 16. Nxe4 loses at least 250 centipawns: White recaptures, ...d5 attacks the knight on e4, and the knight steps back to d2. White has won a knight for a pawn (about +3.2) [V].

feedback_by_move.f6e4: Nxe4 loses at least 250 centipawns (depth 16): White recaptures on e4, ...d5 attacks that knight, and it steps back to d2. White is a knight for a pawn ahead.
